questions.q: Where should the net Sharpe of 0.42 appear in a 10-15 minute SR-5 presentation?
options: Only in the final slide, as a reveal after building suspense
In the first 90 seconds, stated clearly before explaining why it should be believed
It should be omitted and only the gross Sharpe of 0.76 presented
Only in response to a direct question during Q&A
questions.explain: The suggested opening states the net result (0.42 Sharpe) within the first 90 seconds, then spends the rest of the talk building the case for why it should be trusted, rather than building to it as a reveal.

questions.q: In the suggested slide-time allocation, why do the risk and stress-test slides get more combined time than the headline-result slide?
options: Because the headline result is considered unimportant
Because a result without its risk context is the easiest thing in the room to attack or mistrust
Because risk metrics take longer to calculate live
Because the audience is assumed to already know the headline number
questions.explain: The risk profile and stress-test sections get 6 combined minutes versus 2 for the headline result, because risk context is what makes a performance number credible rather than suspect.

questions.q: When presenting the COVID stress-test result, what caveat should be added immediately, without waiting to be asked?
options: That the COVID data was excluded from the backtest
That SR-5's beta to SPY spiked to roughly 0.25 during COVID due to correlation-to-one, even though it still outperformed SPY by a wide margin
That the strategy guarantees similar performance in any future crash
That SPY's performance during COVID is not publicly verifiable
questions.explain: Even though SR-5 outperformed SPY sharply in COVID (-6.1% vs -33.9%), the presentation should immediately note the beta spike to ~0.25 from correlation-to-one, rather than letting the strong relative result stand unqualified.

questions.q: What is the recommended way to handle a question in Q&A you don't know the answer to?
options: Give your best guess confidently so the room doesn't lose trust
Say you don't know and name what you'd need to find out to answer it properly
Change the subject to a prepared talking point
Decline to answer and move to the next question
questions.explain: A confident 'I don't know, here's how I'd check' is recommended over guessing, since a wrong guess that's later discovered costs more credibility than an honest unknown.

questions.q: What closes Chapter 5, and what does Chapter 6 shift to?
options: Chapter 5 closes with raw data collection; Chapter 6 repeats the backtest with new data
Chapter 5 closes the SR-5 project with the live presentation; Chapter 6 shifts to quant job search and interview preparation
Chapter 5 closes with a second stress test; Chapter 6 repeats the presentation for a different audience
Chapter 5 and Chapter 6 both cover SR-5's performance in equal depth
questions.explain: The presentation lesson closes out the SR-5 project and Chapter 5. Chapter 6 moves to general quant career preparation — interviews, resumes, and the recruiting process.
